# ArtCraftMCP > Drive your ArtCraft desktop apps with the OpenCode AI agent — over MCP. [![Windows](https://img.shields.io/badge/Windows-%E2%80%93-blue)](https://github.com/storytold) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode-MCP_Client-purple)](https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/) [![Config](https://img.shields.io/badge/config-1--tab_indent-green)]() [![Servers](https://img.shields.io/badge/servers-19_in_template-brightgreen)]() **New here?** Install in under a minute: double-click `install-opencode-config.bat`, then run `opencode mcp list`. Every app installed on your machine should show green (17 here: 16 ArtCraft + blender). Entries for apps you don't have installed show `failed: system cannot find the path specified` — install the app or delete its block. Details in [troubleshooting](#troubleshooting). --- ## What this is OpenCode is an AI coding agent. ArtCraft apps (WordCraft, VectorCraft, SolidCraft…) each ship a headless CLI that can act as a **Model Context Protocol (MCP) server**. This repo wires them together: one portable `opencode.json` covering **all 19 suite apps** as OpenCode tools, plus a one-click installer that discovers which ones exist on your machine and merges only those into your personal config. **Install — from template to your machine:** ```mermaid flowchart TB TPL["opencode.json\nall 19 suite apps, 1-tab\n'.' roots, no usernames"] BAT["install-opencode-config.bat"] PS1["merge-opencode-config.ps1\ninstall present exes, skip missing\nkeep blender + models, .bak first"] GLB["global opencode.json\ninstalled servers merged\n16 of 19 on this machine"] TPL --> PS1 BAT --> PS1 PS1 --> GLB ``` **Control — from agent to apps to files:** ```mermaid flowchart LR You(["You"]) --> OC["OpenCode agent"] OC -- "stdio" --> AUTO OC -- "stdio" --> SHORT OC -- "stdio" --> ALLOW OC -- "stdio" --> MAIL OC -- "stdio" --> BARE AUTO["automation roots\nword vector photo deck\npdf effect sound\ncad design fig = guessed"] --> Files SHORT["short roots\ntexture material"] --> Files ALLOW["allow-path\nsolidcraft"] --> Files MAIL["files\nmailcraft --files"] --> Files BARE["bare mcp\ngrid film light\ncraft-anything ani"] --> Files Files["project files\n. = launch folder"] -- "tool results" --> OC ``` **Verify — what the list tells you:** ```mermaid flowchart LR L["opencode mcp list"] --> OK["connected\nserver is up"] L --> MISS["failed: cannot find path\napp not installed"] L --> FLAG["failed: unknown option\nwrong flags for that CLI"] ``` In short: **OpenCode finds your apps** — not the other way around. Each entry in `opencode.json` tells OpenCode which executable to launch and which folders it may touch. --- ## What's in this repo | File | What it does | | ---- | ------------ | | `opencode.json` | The portable template — all 19 ArtCraft servers, each with its own sandbox flags, `"."` roots, no hardcoded username. | | `install-opencode-config.bat` | One-click installer. Discovers installed apps, merges them into your global config, backs it up first, then relaunches OpenCode. | | `merge-opencode-config.ps1` | The merge engine behind the `.bat`. Installs only servers whose exe exists on disk, skips the rest, keeps everything else you already had. | All JSON in this repo uses **1-tab indentation** as standard — including everything the merger writes. --- ## Quick start ### Option A — one click (recommended) 1. Double-click **`install-opencode-config.bat`**. 2. It backs up your current global config (`opencode.json..bak`), discovers which suite exes exist (16 of 19 on this machine), merges those in, and restarts OpenCode. 3. Run `opencode mcp list` — every installed app should be green: ```text ✓ anicraft connected ✓ blender connected ✓ craftanything connected ✓ deckcraft connected ✓ effectcraft connected ✓ filmcraft connected ✓ gridcraft connected ✓ lightcraft connected ✓ mailcraft connected ✓ materialcraft connected ✓ pdfcraft connected ✓ photocraft connected ✓ solidcraft connected ✓ soundcraft connected ✓ texturecraft connected ✓ vectorcraft connected ✓ wordcraft connected ``` Your existing setup is safe: the merger **keeps** entries it doesn't know about (like `blender`) and your `model` / `small_model` choices. It only adds or refreshes ArtCraft servers whose exe is actually installed — the rest are reported as skipped and left untouched. Servers for apps you never installed show `✗ failed: system cannot find the path specified`; either install the app or delete its block from your copy. ### Option B — per project Copy `opencode.json` into your project folder (where you launch `opencode` from). Project config overrides global where they overlap. ### Option C — manual merge ```bat powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File merge-opencode-config.ps1 -Repo opencode.json -GlobalPath "%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\opencode.json" opencode mcp list ``` --- ## Prerequisites - **OpenCode installed and on `PATH`.** Check with `opencode --version` in a fresh terminal. If it works there but not in your editor, **restart the editor** so it picks up the new `PATH`. - **ArtCraft apps installed** under `C:\Program Files\\`. The template covers all 19 suite apps; on this machine `CADCraft`, `DesignCraft` and `FigCraft` aren't installed, so the installer skips those three entries. AniCraft ships inside the suite folder (`C:\Program Files\ArtCraft\AniCraft\`) rather than in its own `C:\Program Files\AniCraft\` — the installer looks in both and rewrites the path to whichever exists. - **Windows.** Your global config lives at `%USERPROFILE%\.config\opencode\opencode.json`. --- ## Compatibility matrix Every ArtCraft CLI exposes `mcp`, but each one guards file access with **different flags**. Using the wrong flag is the #1 cause of `✗ failed` lines — 16 entries below were verified against that exe's real `mcp --help` output plus a spawn probe; the last 3 use the most common flag family as a best guess (those apps aren't installed here) and are marked accordingly. | App | Command tail | Flag family | | --- | ------------ | ----------- | | wordcraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | automation roots | | vectorcraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | automation roots | | solidcraft | `mcp --allow-path .` | `--allow-path` (**only SolidCraft**) | | photocraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | automation roots | | gridcraft | `mcp` | bare — no root flags exist | | deckcraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | automation roots | | pdfcraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | automation roots | | filmcraft | `mcp` | bare — headless or `--bridge` | | lightcraft | `mcp` | bare — session flags only | | effectcraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | automation roots | | soundcraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | automation roots | | texturecraft | `mcp --read-root . --write-root .` | short form, **no** `automation-` prefix | | materialcraft | `mcp --read-root . --write-root .` | short form, same dialect as texturecraft | | mailcraft | `mcp --files . --allow mailbox` | `--files DIR` — file sandbox; template also passes `--allow mailbox` so the agent can open mailbox files (send/delete/accounts/settings/input stay gated) | | craftanything | `mcp` | bare — `--allow-run` is code-execution consent, not a path gate | | cadcraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | guessed, unverified — app not installed here | | designcraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | guessed, unverified — app not installed here | | figcraft | `mcp --automation-read-root . --automation-write-root .` | guessed, unverified — app not installed here | | anicraft | `mcp` | bare — no root flags exist; it reads and writes the paths the agent names, with your own permissions | If you install one of those three, confirm its flags first with `"C:\Program Files\\.exe" mcp --help` and correct the template if they differ — then re-run the installer. (`solvecraft-cli.exe` exists on disk but prints "deprecated, use solidcraft-cli", so it has no entry.) Two layout notes for AniCraft: its CLI lives in the suite folder (`C:\Program Files\ArtCraft\AniCraft\anicraft-cli.exe`), not in a `C:\Program Files\AniCraft\` of its own, and the installer rewrites the entry to whichever of the two paths it finds. Its server also takes an optional document argument — `mcp` opens an empty one, `mcp --sample` opens the bundled sample, `mcp scene.anicraft` opens yours — so the template stays on the bare `mcp`. --- ## App sources on GitHub Almost everything official lives under [@storytold](https://github.com/storytold) (the ArtCraft org, [getartcraft.com](https://getartcraft.com)) — each app has its own repo with releases, docs and an issue tracker. The exceptions are SolidCraft, a community app by [Tangency Labs](https://github.com/tangency-labs), and MailCraft, a community app ([ZIDAN44/mailcraft](https://github.com/ZIDAN44/mailcraft)). Found a wrong flag or a new app release that changed the CLI? Open an issue in the app's repo above, or in [this repo](https://github.com/xevilmaxx/ArtCraftMCP/issues). --- ## File access, simply explained Each headless server is **sandboxed**: with no root flag it can't read or write your project files (symptom: SolidCraft saves landing in `Temp\solidcraft-mcp-…` with "Save to Downloads is blocked"). The template grants access with `"."`: - **Portable** — no `C:\Users\` inside, works for every user and checkout. - **Follows you** — `"."` means "wherever you launched OpenCode". - **Recursive** — subfolders like `.\projects\designs\part1.sc` are covered. - **Repeatable** — most CLIs accept the flag more than once for several folders. Need wider access? Replace `"."` with an absolute folder on the servers you want to widen. Prefer the smallest scope that works. **AniCraft is the exception.** Its `mcp` server has no root flags at all — there is no sandbox to widen. It reads and writes the paths the agent names, with your own permissions, so scope it by asking for work inside a project folder. The engine's own guard is the `confirm: true` that destructive commands demand before they replace a file. --- ## Usage ```bat opencode opencode mcp list opencode run "Export the current VectorCraft canvas to SVG" opencode run --quiet "Parse input vectors from build/out.svg and feed coordinates to the cutting engine RPC on localhost:9000" ``` Headless, without MCP: ```bat "C:\Program Files\WordCraft\wordcraft-cli.exe" run --file doc.docx --cmd "caret.docEnd" --save out.docx --print ``` --- ## Troubleshooting
opencode isn't installed or isn't on your PATH Run `opencode --version` in a **new** terminal. "Not recognized" means OpenCode isn't installed or its folder isn't in system `PATH`. If it works in a terminal but not inside your editor or the Craft Anything extension, **restart the IDE** — it inherited the old environment. Some extensions also have a setting for the explicit opencode binary path.
'wordcraft-mcp-executable' is not recognized… That name is a placeholder from generic docs — no such binary exists. Point `command` at the real exe, e.g. `["C:\Program Files\WordCraft\wordcraft-cli.exe", "mcp", …]`. Keep each argument as its own JSON array element, especially paths with spaces.
Every server shows ✗ failed … unknown option '--allow-path' `--allow-path` is SolidCraft-only. The other CLIs reject it (craft-anything even suggests `--allow-run`, which is unrelated — it gates code execution, not folders). Fix: use this repo's `opencode.json`, which carries the per-app flags from the [matrix](#compatibility-matrix), re-run the installer, then `opencode mcp list`.
Saves land in Temp, destination "blocked" The server's sandbox doesn't include your destination. Either launch OpenCode in the destination's parent (roots are `"."`), or add that folder as a root flag for the server, then restart OpenCode so the server respawns with the new flags.
Port already in use (opencode mcp list, opencode reload) / shows nothing A stale `opencode` background service is holding managed-service port 28894, so any command needing the service fails with `Failed to start server. Is port 28894 in use?`. Right after killing it, the first command may briefly say `No MCP servers configured` while the service reboots — just run it again. Find the squatter and stop just that process: ```bat powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 28894 | Select-Object OwningProcess" taskkill /F /PID opencode mcp list ```
✗ failed: The system cannot find the path specified That app isn't installed where the template expects (`C:\Program Files\\.exe`). This is normal for `cadcraft`, `designcraft` and `figcraft` on machines without them — and for any app when you run `opencode mcp list` from inside this repo (the repo template itself lists all 19 as project config). Either install the missing app or delete its block from your copy of `opencode.json`. For AniCraft, check the suite folder too: the CLI is at `C:\Program Files\ArtCraft\AniCraft\anicraft-cli.exe`, and the installer relocates the entry automatically if only that path exists.
My blender server / model settings disappeared That was the old installer, which **overwrote** the global file. The current one **merges** and writes a timestamped `.bak` first. Restore from the `.bak` next to your global config, then run the new installer.
--- ## References - OpenCode config & precedence (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, project `opencode.json`, `OPENCODE_CONFIG` overrides) — [opencode.ai/docs/config](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/) - MCP servers (`type: local` + `command`, optional `cwd` / `environment` / `timeout`) — [opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers](https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/) - The `--allow-path`-everywhere claim from an earlier AI troubleshooting thread is **wrong** — 16 of the 19 [matrix](#compatibility-matrix) entries were verified exe-by-exe (the other 3 use the most common flag family as a guess), and `opencode mcp list` reports every installed server connected.
